q: What is the difference between a contract and a promise?
r: A contract is legally enforceable because it has required elements
Courts enforce valid contracts.
w: A contract is always spoken and a promise is always written
Form does not define the difference.
A promise is enforced by the government and a contract is not
There is no difference in any situation

q: A company installs security cameras that record employees in a restroom. Which legal concern is most relevant?
r: Employee privacy rights
Some areas carry a high expectation of privacy.

q: Which is an example of intellectual property?
r: A software program written by a company
Creations of the mind can be protected.

q: What is the purpose of consumer protection laws?
r: To protect buyers from unfair or unsafe practices
They support fair markets.
w: They are not designed for profit.
To prevent consumers from returning products

q: A restaurant serves food that makes customers ill because it violated health codes. What is the likely consequence?
r: Fines, closure or lawsuits
Health violations bring penalties and liability.

q: What does 'statute of limitations' mean?
r: A time limit for bringing a legal claim
After the period, the claim may be barred.
w: A limit on a company's profits
A limit on the number of employees

q: A business signs a contract but later learns the other party lied about important facts. What may the business be able to do?
r: Seek to cancel the contract or claim damages
Fraud can make a contract voidable.
w: Nothing, because contracts can never be changed
Force the other party to hire them
That does not address the lie.

q: Why must businesses keep accurate employment records?
r: To comply with wage, tax and labor laws
Records show legal compliance.

q: What is an unfair labor practice?
r: An employer action that interferes with workers' legal rights
Labor laws protect organizing and fair treatment.
w: A worker taking a lunch break

q: A company discovers its product label claims it is 'all natural' when it contains artificial ingredients. What should it do?
r: Correct the label and stop false claims
Labels must be truthful.
w: Keep the label because it sells well

q: What is the purpose of a business memo?
r: To share short internal information or instructions
Memos are brief and direct.
w: To send a formal contract to a customer

q: A speaker's slides contain full paragraphs of small text. What is the likely problem?
r: The audience may read instead of listening
Slides should be brief.
w: The audience will remember every word
The slides will be more persuasive
Slides will not need a speaker

q: Which is an example of oral communication?
r: A phone call with a customer
Spoken words are oral.

q: How can you make a business presentation more engaging?
r: Use clear visuals, examples and eye contact
Engagement keeps attention.
w: Read the slides word for word

q: A manager sends a long email with several important requests in one paragraph. What is the best way to improve it?
r: Use short paragraphs, bullet points and a clear subject line
Structure improves clarity.

q: What does 'tone' refer to in writing?
r: The attitude conveyed by word choice and style
Tone affects how a message is received.

q: What is the role of a call to action in a message?
r: To tell the reader what to do next
It guides response.
w: To end the message without a request
To list the sender's job history
That is not a call to action.

q: An employee must respond to a customer in another country with different customs. Which approach is best?
r: Research local customs and adapt tone and style respectfully
Cultural awareness avoids offense.
w: Assume all customers want the same style
Use slang the customer may not know

q: What is a service level agreement?
r: A document defining the level of service a customer can expect
It sets measurable standards.

q: A customer thanks a store employee for remembering her name and past purchases. Which tool supports this kind of service?
r: A customer relationship management system
It stores customer history.

q: Why does a business monitor online reviews?
r: To learn what customers think and respond to concerns
Reviews influence reputation.
w: To reduce the number of customers

q: It costs a company five times more to win a new customer than to keep an existing one. What should the company prioritize?
r: Programs that keep current customers satisfied
Retention is cost effective.

q: What is a customer persona?
r: A profile of a typical customer's needs and traits
It helps tailor service and marketing.

q: What is the best way to end a customer interaction?
r: Thank the customer and ask if there is anything else
It leaves a positive impression.
w: Ask for a tip every time

q: A company discovers that customers wait on hold 12 minutes. What improvement would best help service?
r: Add staff or offer callback and chat options
Reducing waits improves satisfaction.

q: A factory buys machines that let each worker make twice as many items per hour. What increased?
r: Labor productivity
Output per worker rose.

q: What does supply refer to?
r: The quantity of a good sellers are willing to offer at each price
Supply generally rises with price.
w: The amount buyers want at each price

q: What is market equilibrium?
r: The price at which quantity supplied equals quantity demanded
The market clears.
w: The point where sellers refuse to sell
A price set by government only
A time when demand is zero

q: A price ceiling set below the equilibrium price on apartments will most likely cause:
r: A shortage of apartments
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

q: What is entrepreneurship's role in an economy?
r: Creating new businesses, jobs and innovation
It drives growth.

q: Which is most likely to cause inflation?
r: Demand rising faster than supply
Too much spending chasing few goods raises prices.
w: A fall in the money supply

q: What does comparative advantage mean?
r: The ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost
It guides specialization and trade.
w: Producing more of every good than others
Selling at a higher price always

q: What is active collaboration?
r: Working with others to share ideas and reach common goals
It uses everyone's strengths.

q: A new employee makes a mistake that costs the company money. Which response from a leader builds trust and learning?
r: Discuss what happened, learn from it and provide support
Learning environments improve performance.
w: Fire the employee immediately in all cases

q: Why does self-awareness matter at work?
r: Knowing your strengths and weaknesses helps you improve
It guides growth.
w: It prevents you from receiving feedback
It removes the need for goals

q: Which action demonstrates ethical behavior?
r: Reporting an accounting error even if it benefits you
Ethics means honesty over advantage.
w: Hiding the error to keep a bonus
Blaming a coworker for the error
Waiting for someone else to find it

q: Employees are resisting a new software system. What should a leader do to ease the change?
r: Explain the benefits, listen to concerns and provide training
Support reduces resistance.

q: A founder asks 100 potential customers about a product idea and most say they would not buy it. What should she do?
r: Reconsider or change the idea based on the feedback
Feedback reduces risk.
w: Ignore the answers and launch anyway

q: What is revenue for a new business?
r: Money earned from selling products or services
It is income before expenses.

q: Why do entrepreneurs seek a mentor or advisor?
r: To gain experience and advice
Guidance can prevent mistakes.

q: What is a line of credit?
r: A set amount of money a borrower can use as needed
Interest applies to the amount used.

q: A company's current assets are $60,000 and current liabilities are $30,000. What is its current ratio?
What is the purpose of insurance?
r: To protect against financial loss from risks
Premiums pool risk.
w: To increase the chance of loss
To pay all of a person's bills

q: A person invests $500 at 6% compound interest for 2 years. About how much will she have?
r: $500 times 1.06 squared.
w: That is one year of simple interest.

q: A department has many open jobs and low morale. Which HR action would best address both?
r: Improve recruiting while gathering feedback to fix workplace issues
Both hiring and culture matter.

q: What is succession planning?
r: Preparing employees to fill key roles in the future
It ensures continuity.

q: What is malware?
r: Software designed to harm or steal from a computer
Viruses are an example.
w: Software that speeds up a computer

q: A company stores customer credit card numbers in a plain text file anyone can open. What is the main risk?
r: Data theft and misuse
Unprotected data is vulnerable.

q: What is a spreadsheet formula used for?
r: Performing calculations automatically
It updates when data changes.

q: What is direct marketing?
r: Communicating directly with targeted customers, such as by email
It aims for a measurable response.

q: A company wants to know if a new ad increased sales. What should it compare?
r: Sales before and after the ad
Comparison shows impact.

q: What is a slogan?
r: A short phrase that expresses a brand's message
It helps customers remember the brand.

q: What is a bill of materials?
r: A list of parts and materials needed to make a product
It supports production planning.

q: A call center wants to reduce customer wait times without lowering service quality. Which approach is best?
r: Analyze call volume patterns and schedule staff accordingly
Data-driven scheduling helps.

q: What is a warehouse used for?
r: Storing goods until they are sold or shipped
It supports distribution.

q: Why is it useful to set short-term goals?
r: They break larger goals into manageable steps
Progress builds motivation.
w: They remove the need for long-term goals

q: During an interview, you are asked about a weakness. What is the best approach?
r: Name a real weakness and explain how you are improving
Honesty with action shows growth.

q: A manager wants to reduce risk when launching a new product. Which action is most effective?
r: Test the product in a small market first
Pilot testing limits exposure.
w: Launch in every market at once
